questions.question: Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder with radius r and height h =
questions.explanation: CSA of cylinder = 2πrh. This is the lateral surface (the curved part only, like the label on a can). TSA = CSA + 2 circular bases = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r). Volume = πr²h.

If the radius of a cylinder is doubled (height unchanged), volume becomes:
questions.explanation: V = πr²h. New radius = 2r. New V = π(2r)²h = 4πr²h = 4V. Volume becomes 4 times. (Area scales as r², so doubling radius quadruples volume when height is constant.)

A metal rod (cylinder) of r = 1 cm, length = 100 cm is melted and recast as a cylinder of r = 2 cm. New length =
questions.explanation: Volume conserved when melted and recast. π×1²×100 = π×2²×h → 100 = 4h → h = 25 cm. (Doubling radius and keeping volume same → height ÷ 4.)

Compare a cylinder (r = 7, h = 14) and a cuboid (7 × 14 × 14). Which has greater volume? (π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Cylinder: V = πr²h = (22/7)×49×14 = 22×7×14 = 2,156 cm³. Cuboid: V = 7×14×14 = 1,372 cm³. Cylinder (2,156) > Cuboid (1,372). For the same height and similar base dimensions, a cylinder generally has greater volume than a rectangular box.
